crime.value: Murder of young woman Darathea Mondragon in July 1985; body found with torn clothes and broken neck in remote location. Central question: who killed her and left semen evidence at the scene?
crime.quote: Her neck is broken. She is dead... a semen sample found on the body of Darathea Mondragon

victim.value: Darathea Mondragon, young hitchhiker traveling from El Paso to Boulder, Colorado. Vulnerable hitchhiker dependent on rides from strangers.
victim.quote: Darathea Mondragon waits by the road in El Paso with her thumb out... and a different person offers a lift

culprit_and_motive.value: Convicted rapist serving 99 years at Los Lunas penitentiary; DNA match from semen sample. Motive: sexual assault and murder.
culprit_and_motive.quote: a semen sample found on the body... DNA corresponding with that of a convicted rapist currently serving ninety-nine years

resolution.value: Detective Henderson uses modern DNA forensic methods (cheek swab, hair sample) which are tested and compared against database, exonerating Kent and identifying the true perpetrator who confesses.
resolution.quote: Detective Henderson... slid a swab over the inside of Kent's cheek... Laboratory tests proved conclusively that a semen sample... had DNA corresponding with... a convicted rapist

investigator.value: Detective Henderson, modern police investigator using forensic DNA technology; also implicitly Kent, the wrongly accused suspect whose perspective frames the narrative.
investigator.quote: Detective Henderson (despite his name, three-quarters Hispanic) had a degree in penology from UNM and wanted to prove the value of modern methods of police work

suspect_architecture.value: Single primary suspect (Kent, the trucker) repeatedly targeted by authorities over 16 years; actual perpetrator is an unnamed convicted rapist serving 99 years at Los Lunas — architecture is one innocent man falsely suspected versus one guilty man hidden offscreen until DNA reveal.
suspect_architecture.quote: a semen sample found on the body of Darathea Mondragon had DNA corresponding with that of a convicted rapist currently serving ninety-nine years

red_herring.value: The curandera's staged 'vision' session, orchestrated by detectives, is designed to make Kent appear guilty by eliciting incriminating-sounding confessions; his tearful 'yes' responses and 'it's my fault' misdirect toward guilt when he in fact only witnessed the aftermath of his own innocent presence near the scene.
red_herring.quote: They were the ones who had pressured Maria de Guadalupe, threatening to have her deported as an illegal, and had orchestrated the episode.

clue_fairness.value: The reader is given Kent's internal account of July 1985 — he parked, ate, smoked, and never touched Darathea — simultaneously with the detectives' coerced 'confession'; the exculpatory DNA evidence is broadcast on public TV news, available to Kent and reader at the same moment.
clue_fairness.quote: He had never touched her... Laboratory tests proved conclusively that a semen sample found on the body of Darathea Mondragon had DNA

social_world.value: Layered immigrant/working-class hierarchy in New Mexico: undocumented Latino workers exploitable by police deportation threats, Anglo laborers like Kent marginally more protected, wealthy spa clients at the top; institutional police power wielded against the vulnerable regardless of guilt.
social_world.quote: the Latino employees — semilegals from Mexico and El Salvador — never took advantage of this offer, being in a hurry to get back

alibi.value: Kent's alibi is his own internal memory: he stopped to eat a tamale, smoke a joint, drink a Dr Pepper, and never touched the victim — confirmed ultimately by DNA exonerating him; his 'it's my fault' confession refers only to his coincidental presence enabling the real killer's opportunity.
alibi.quote: 'I never touched her.' ... 'It's my fault,' he said. 'It's all your fault,' the bruja echoed.

reveal_mechanic.value: DNA forensic testing — a cheek swab and a single scalp hair collected by Detective Henderson — matches the semen found on the victim to a convicted rapist already in prison, definitively exonerating Kent; the solution is demonstrated scientifically and broadcast as a brief TV news item.
reveal_mechanic.quote: Henderson did not handcuff the suspect... he put on latex gloves and requested Kent to open his mouth. Then Henderson slid a swab over the inside of Kent's cheek

media_and_audience.value: The crime's resolution is packaged as a minor TV news filler item — sandwiched between an Afghanistan war story and a human-interest joke piece about 'Mary Christmas' — trivialising 16 years of wrongful suspicion; the case's public significance is minimal, reflecting institutional indifference to working-class victims and suspects.
media_and_audience.quote: just a short piece, after the serious story from Afghanistan and before the humorous spot about a woman in Penasco whose name really is Mary Christmas

investigator_wound.value: Maria de Guadalupe (the curandera-as-reluctant-investigator) carries guilt for having been coerced into entrapping an innocent man under threat of deportation; her wound is complicity through vulnerability, resolved only when she offers Kent wordless absolution at the story's close.
investigator_wound.quote: the fortuneteller — her eyes screwed up but without tears — said, 'I'm sorry, so sorry, please forgive me,' to the man who was being hauled out
